newsitem.title: USA: Calaveras County, Calif, district defaults on debt.
newsitem.headline: Calaveras County, Calif, district defaults on debt.

text.p: The Calaveras County, Calif., Water District has defaulted on a September payment of interest and principal to holders of over $8.7 million of outstanding assessment district debt, officials said Thursday.

The district, as expected, missed the September 2 payment. It also defaulted on March 2 on the regularly scheduled payment of interest on these bonds because of the high rate of property developer delinquencies in the assessment district.
The district sold $9.68 million of limited obligation improvement bonds in 1991. As of March 2, 1996, about $8.74 million of the bonds were still outstanding.

Although some additional funds have been received in recent months, there was only $80,000 in the bond reserve fund available to pay the $350,000 which became due on March 2 and the $647,000 that was due on September 2, district advisor Robert Doty said.
The district said the assessment delinquency rate increased sharply to 85 percent last December, reducing the already severely diminished cash flow.
The water district was expected to schedule a public hearing to make the determination of whether there will be an ultimate loss to the bondholders.
In the meantime, the district said it was forming a team to evaluate various options for a financial workout of the obligations.
